findings.subject: scrollable-list
findings.summary: Activating a chevron scroll control can unmount the focused button, dropping keyboard focus to <body>; its labels are fixed English and the list has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/scrollable-list/scrollable-list.tsx:272-311 renders each control only while canScrollStart/canScrollEnd; :280,:301 aria-label literals; :18-41 no aria-label prop
findings.fix: Keep both controls mounted and set disabled/aria-disabled (or move focus to the remaining control) when an edge is reached; add labels props (scrollStartLabel/scrollEndLabel) and spread rest props so aria-label reaches the root; add a test that focus survives the last scroll.

verified.reason: I checked scrollable-list.tsx and the claim matches the code. Both chevron Buttons sit inside `{showChevrons && canScrollStart/End && !disabled && ...}` (lines 272-311), so the control unmounts when the scroll reaches that edge. A keyboard user who presses 'Scroll right' until the end therefore loses the focused element. Nothing in the component handles focus: no focus or ref handoff, no visibility- or inert-based hiding (the CSS only uses display:flex). The test file has no test of focus after the last scroll. The aria-labels 'Scroll left' and 'Scroll right' are literals that change only with RTL, and the props interface (lines 18-41) has no label or i18n prop and no ...rest, so adopters cannot localize them or name the list. The missing accessible name is the weakest part, because a plain div does not strictly need one. The focus loss and the fixed English labels alone are a real K2 focus-management and naming gap for a beta-supported component, so P1 stands.
